Bloatware. Don’t get me wrong the app will get you results but that’s not what we’re reviewing here. We’re rating the app. 

It used to be a great app. And it still could be, if you can tolerate all the animations and extra bloat. Ironically, for a weight loss app, it’s become a bit bloatware itself.

If there were an option to subscribe to a stripped down version focused just on food tracking, and weigh-ins I’d sign up in a heart beat. I don’t need the animations, I don’t need to redo the course, and I don’t need ll the extra fluff. I just want a clean, simple way to track what I eat, because that part of the app is genuinely the best I’ve used!

reviews.text: Too gamified now. This is my second time doing Noom, the first time was a great success, and this time around started off great with a bang. But then an update hit the app a couple of months ago that made it nearly unusable. The gamification has been taken to the extreme and it seems like I can’t log a meal without 5 pop-ups to shower me with affirmation, seeds, and lightning bolts, and then another pop up to encourage me to chase some other token. Noom as a program and a system works, I can follow the system but to do so I need to log meals without it taking an eternity and making me cringe. There should be a setting or settings in the app to disable some of those over-the-top features, especially for people like me who are not particularly wired psychologically to respond to affirmation and praise, and don’t need gamification and token-seeking to stay motivated. Results motivate me and right now it’s hard to chase those results with an utterly unusable app.

Not so innovative anymore. The psychology is good but the biggest place where Noom is failing its paid subscribers is there is no fiber tracking. In 2026 when fiber & protein are what we are being told is most important, we can’t track both with a $200 subscription? When so many of us are on GLP-1s?Customer service just blows me off on if/when Fiber will will be available.

The food tracking database is duplicative and out of date. Some items I added were never included while there can be five or more similar brand name products with wrong macros or calories. Reports of problems appear to be ignored. I don’t know what is going on with this company.

The body scan which ostensibly provides measurements is not ready for prime time. The data jumps from scan to scan and does not reflect the consistent weight loss tracked in Noom. It’s really frustrating.

I have not decided yet what I’m going to do about my subscription. For now I have deactivated auto renew. Unless fiber tracking is implemented, I will probably save some money and go with a different app.

 Note: All my concerns have been communicated to Noom and they have not been responsive except for the equivalent of a chirpy marketing “Sorry!”.

reviews.text:
Color system messing with my feelings of success. The color system is psychologically misleading. Staying within calorie goals and eating healthy foods can still feel like failure because one color category goes over while another remains underfilled. Unused calories from one category should dynamically redistribute instead of leaving empty sections that visually imply goals weren’t met. The current design feels unintentionally discouraging even on healthy eating days. I feel more guilty for eating a cup of lentils than a chocolate chip cookie because I went over on yellow foods and didn’t fulfill my orange food “goals.” It becomes a psychological issue, which is ironic considering the program is based on psychology.
I also found it surprisingly difficult to access basic information about which foods belong in each color category. I was trying to figure out whether a snack fit within my goals and couldn’t readily find the information. It took me two days to finally locate it. When I used the help chat, it sent me links that didn’t work, and after I explained that the links were broken, I just received a generic apology instead of actual help. That was incredibly frustrating. Information this important should be much easier for users to access since the entire program revolves around staying within these categories and calorie goals.
At this point, I’m not sure this is the right weight loss app for me.

Disappointed. “Psychology based” so long as your answers to quizzes fit the ones they provide, I guess.

I am currently at a fairly healthy weight, but I’m struggling with an impulse control issue. Given that Noom talks about using psychology to address eating patterns, I figured I’d give it a try. I deleted it before the free trial period ended. 

First, it threw me off to be offered probiotics before the app knew anything about me. I guess it just assumes everyone should be buying that product. I don’t need it, so it felt like a profit center more than sound nutritional advice. 

The bigger issue was that the app didn’t give me the opportunity to adequately explain my situation. My impulse control issue is related to ADHD. I’ve always struggled with it, but I was just diagnosed as having ADHD about 18 months ago. Unfortunately, I’m allergic to the stimulants that best treat ADHD. I’m currently on a non-stimulant prescription. It’s nowhere near as effective, and I’m back to having frequent evening binge eating sessions. I was hopeful Noom would help me address this behavior and give me workable solutions. 
The first issue came up with the quizzes. I encountered questions for which none of the given answers were even close, and there was no option to choose “other” or to write my own answer. 
I tried to use the help function. I got the AI bot. It asked me to upload a screenshot. I am a competent iPhone user, and I could not find a way to upload a screenshot. The bot told me it would connect me with a coach. I waited several minutes. I then replied “I can’t keep waiting on a response as I have other things I need to do.” 
I tried again, but I ran into the same issue with quizzes. Same runaround with the bot. 
Several days later, I found a bunch of emails in my junk mail folder. Tech support had contacted me by email. I didn’t know they had, so I didn’t go looking for an email. 
I replied even though I’d already deleted the app. I explained my situation with the quiz answers that are available didn’t match my situation at all, and that the bot wanted me to upload a screenshot but I couldn’t see how to do it. They replied, telling me that sounded like something that needed to be addressed by a coach… 
I imagine the stock answers the app allows a user to choose work for the majority of people. I’m not one of them, though.

The app that was supposed to make managing my health easier has become a barrier to care. I would not recommend Noom’s medication management program to anyone.

Then, it gives me immediate feedback. It doesn't just tell me the calories. The automated coach gives me feedback on how I could improve my meal to make it healthier. The daily Noom educational materials also include psychological tips and tricks to help me stick to my plan. I feel a little bit silly admitting this, but the program also gives me little "atta boy" positive feedback that even makes it fun. Altogether, I do recommend Noom even though it's a bit expensive for me. If it's going to help my help in the long run and works when other things didn't, it's worth the invest investment.
